programs.title: Working as one: Three Chinese villages pool resources for shared growth
programs.desc: Three villages in Shandong run on one shared economic ledger. It is a rural experiment in resource re‑allocation, pointing to alternative possibilities for rural communities across the developing world. In this episode of BizFocus, CGTN anchor Lincoln Humphries explores three villages in Dezhou, Shandong for their stories.

programs.title: The AI revolution is here - but are we ready for what comes next?
programs.desc: In this special joint episode of World Economic Forum and CGTN, hosts Robin Pomeroy from World Economic Forum and Guan Xin, CGTN Anchor, sit down with Professor Arun Sundararajan of New York University's Stern School of Business, a member of the WEF AI Governance Alliance and author of The Sharing Economy. They dive into the most pressing questions about artificial intelligence. From the future of employment to the deepening divide over AI governance and technological sovereignty, this conversation brings together perspectives from the US, China, and the global stage on how AI is reshaping economies, societies, and geopolitics.

Chinese buyers are spending more on lighter, trendier gold pieces
programs.desc: Gold jewelry consumption in China has seen a significant shift in recent times. Weight and high prices, once the prime market movers, are no longer the main drivers. Buyers are shifting to lighter pieces, while heritage craft and youth design are creating new reasons to buy.

programs.title: Inside the world’s first robot-staffed theme park
programs.desc: China has just opened what's billed as the world's first large-scale robot theme park in the southern city of Zhuhai – more than 300 humanoid robots working the floor. It's a debut for an industry that's raised billions but is still hunting for a commercial win.

programs.title: How tea factories are brewing new consumption
programs.desc: Who would travel to a factory just to watch tea being made? Turns out, quite a few people. In China’s tea producing county of Anxi, tea factories are opening their doors to tourists. CGTN reporter Yu Bokun sees how they are turning production lines into attractions, and visitors into potential customers.

programs.title: How China's ocean kingdom makes billions
China's Kungfu theme park: A wild ride back in time
programs.desc: At Wansuishan Martial Arts City in central China’s Kaifeng, Henan Province, you’re not just a visitor - you’re part of the story. Every segment in the park is part of an immersive experience rooted in Chinese martial arts and traditional culture. From live matchmaking shows to iron flower performances, from Song Dynasty streets to interactive stages, this uniquely Chinese theme park – with not even one roller coaster or scary ride – was able to record over 24 million visits in 2025.

programs.title: Bizfocus: From myth to reality: How tech brings Eastern imagination to life
programs.desc: Ever wondered what China’s version of “Adam and Eve” or “Beauty and the Beast” looks like? While the world’s theme parks are all about Western fairy tales, one Chinese park took a different path—Fantawild brings ancient Eastern myths to life with mind-blowing tech and art. In this episode of Bizfocus, CGTN’s Xu Yi and her new friends from Pakistan and Bangladesh go for adventure in Fantawild Oriental Heritage in Mianyang, Sichuan. Gods, legends, and the tech behind the magic—all in one epic trip.

programs.title: NAVIGATING GLOBAL ECONOMIC CHANGE | Exclusive with WEF President
programs.desc: The year 2026 marks the 20th anniversary of the establishment of the World Economic Forum's Beijing Representative Office. CGTN's Guan Xin speaks with Alois Zwinggi, president and CEO of WEF, to look back on nearly five decades of cooperation between WEF and China, examine the future of globalization and explore how 'China Opportunity 2.0' can further advance global cooperation in supply chain resilience, green technology and AI governance.

programs.title: Tennis Australia exec on the Australian Open's China push
programs.desc: China is taking center court in the Australian Open's global growth strategy. The Grand Slam has kicked off its 2027 China campaign in Beijing, aiming to engage fans through localized digital content, live events, retail and Chinese cultural Ambassadors. Tennis Australia says its long-term investment is paying off, with China now one of the tournament's largest international markets.

programs.title: Farmed with China: Malaysia's rice has a secret superpower
programs.desc: Despite its fertile tropical landscape, Malaysia produces only around two-thirds of the rice it needs. Chinese ratoon rice technology is now being applied to lift yields and enhance food security—unlocking new potential for tropical farming. Discover more in CGTN's special series #FarmedwithChina. #Chinavsionary

Farmed with China: Thailand's farms go high-tech
programs.desc: As labor grows scarce, how can the land still yield abundant harvests? China-Thailand cooperation is providing solutions: machines for farmers, jobs in factories, and training for young agricultural engineers. Technology is more than equipment — it brings efficiency and hope.

programs.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!
programs.desc: Rice and prawn grow better together. Prawn loosens the soil and control pests, while rice cleans and oxygenates the water. One field, two harvests. A team from Shanghai Ocean University brought this eco-farming model to Cambodia, helping turn rice paddies into new sources of income.
